newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil Tigers attack Sri Lanka government air base.
newsitem.headline: Tamil Tigers attack Sri Lanka government air base.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels launched a three-hour attack on an air force base in Sri Lanka's eastern Trincomalee district and damaged one transport plane before being repelled, police said on Thursday.

They said about 300 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels attacked the China Bay base about 240 km (150 miles) east of the capital Colombo with mortars and rocket launchers late on Wednesday.
Initial reports said one person was killed and several wounded in the attack which began at about 11.30 p.m. (1730 GMT).
Military sources said the transport plane was damaged slightly by mortars launched by the rebels.
Air force and military officials were not immediately available for comment. An LTTE spokesman in London also could not be reached.
The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese island's north and east.
Last year, the LTTE overran a key army base on the northeast coast, killing or capturing the camp's 1,000 men and dealing the the military its worst blow of the war.
In January, the rebels again attacked a military base at Paranthan, a key road junction south of Jaffna. The army said 223 soldiers were killed and the rebels said they lost at least 140.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the 13-year-old war. The LTTE says the number is higher.
